title: Dribble Handoff Continuity
description: Players practise the dribble handoff — a soft pass delivered while both players are moving — as a continuous team-offense action.

content.objective: Deliver and receive a clean, well-timed dribble handoff while both players are moving.
content.setup: A ball handler dribbles toward a teammate curling to meet them near the wing.
instructions: The ball handler dribbles toward the cutter, timing the approach to meet them.
Hand the ball off softly at the moment of the exchange, not a hard pass.
The receiver attacks immediately off the handoff, either driving or shooting.
The player who gave the handoff screens briefly for the receiver before clearing out.
coachingPoints: Time the handoff so both players arrive at the same spot together.
Keep the exchange soft and controlled, not a thrown pass.
The receiver should attack with purpose immediately, not pause after the catch.
commonMistakes: Handing off too early or late, forcing an awkward catch.
Receiver standing still after the handoff instead of attacking.
Standing still after a pass instead of moving with purpose.
content.safety: Keep the exchange area clear so both players can move freely.
